version.changelog: Add source metadata for installation review

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and required artifacts are coherent with its stated purpose (automating Shanghai Library seat bookings); nothing in the package appears to ask for unrelated credentials or unexpected network endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Shanghai Library seat booking) align with included code: Node.js CLI, API wrappers targeting yuyue.library.sh.cn, login automation via Playwright, and profile-based auth storage. Required capabilities (reading/writing profile files, opening a browser for login, calling the library's API) match the claimed features.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts describe only actions needed for booking: prompting or automating browser login, extracting accessToken/sign/timestamp, saving profiles under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking, and calling the library APIs. I did not find instructions to read unrelated system files, environment secrets, or to transmit data to third-party endpoints beyond the library API.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry lists no automated install spec (instruction-only), but the package includes package.json and depends on playwright. SKILL.md instructs users to install Playwright (npm install / npx playwright install chromium). Playwright is from the public npm registry (package.json references it), not a hidden download. This is expected for browser automation but requires the user to run npm / npx manually; the skill will not auto-download arbitrary binaries from unknown servers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested by the skill. The only persistent secrets are library auth tokens (accessToken, sign, timestamp) which the tool reads/writes to profile files under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking — this is necessary for the described functionality and is explicitly documented in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It persists only its own profile files under a clearly documented directory (default ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/). It launches a local browser via Playwright for login when needed; that behavior is consistent with the stated feature set.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears coherent and does what it says: it automates Shanghai Library seat booking by performing browser-assisted login (Playwright) and calling the library's API. Before installing/running it, consider: 1) You will need Node.js (>=18) and Playwright (npx playwright install chromium) — installing Playwright downloads browser binaries. 2) The script will create and read profile files containing your library auth tokens under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/ — protect those files (SKILL.md suggests chmod 600). 3) The login flow automates a local browser session and extracts tokens after you manually sign in; you should review login.js/login_and_get_auth_node.js if you want to confirm exactly what is extracted. 4) The code only communicates with the documented library domain (yuyue.library.sh.cn); if you see the scripts modified to call other domains or to exfiltrate data, do not run them. If you are not comfortable running third-party code that will execute locally and store authentication tokens, run the commands in a controlled environment or inspect the code locally before use.
